recommendation_summary: The reply says to drop Kafka, CQRS and Redis and instead ask PostgreSQL for the unpaid-invoice count inside the existing endpoint, returning only the number. It offers no optional additions. It does not suggest checking end-to-end latency or confirming the new count matches the old one, though the rubric doesn't require either.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You need the unpaid-invoice count to finish within one second and match invoices committed at request time. You asked which Kafka services and topics to ship this week for a CQRS projection and Redis, because that cluster budget is approved and peers are moving to event-driven systems.
labels.Deleted: Kafka, CQRS, Redis, and any new service or topic. The approved budget and peer trend are not requirements for this count, and a projection is not the committed data at request time.
labels.Bottleneck: The endpoint loads invoice rows, builds invoice objects, and counts them in memory. The wait is that work; PostgreSQL already stores the committed invoices.
labels.Checked myself: I was told there is one application and PostgreSQL, the endpoint returns only this count and has no other reader, and users report the count is slow. I did not inspect the code or the database.

note: All four record lines come before a clear recommendation to count in the database, and the Deleted line removes the Kafka/CQRS/Redis stack by name.
